Heard Sri.Girish B Baladare learned counsel for the appellants as well as Sri.Mallikarjuna
Reddy.N.A.

learned counsel who represents Sri.Pradeep.B learned counsel on record for respondent No.1.
2.

This is a claimants' appeal challenging the order passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Arakalagud in MVC No.628/2021, dated 21.03.2023.

The first appellant in the capacity of the Vanajakshi vs The Manager on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45757814/
2 mother and second appellant in the capacity of the younger brother of the deceased Chandu alias Chandunaika (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased' for brevity) filed a petition claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs,19,75,500/- as compensation and aggrieved by the same, an appeal is preferred.

3. Arguing the matter Sri.Girish B Baladare submits that the deceased by doing coolie work was earning Rs.30,000/- per month but the Tribunal took the notional NC: 2024:KHC:31903 income as Rs.10,000/- per month which is highly unjustifiable.

Learned counsel submits that the accident occurred in the year 2020 and for the relevant period, even Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is taking notional income as Rs.14,500/- per month and thus, atleast the said figure should have been considered by the Tribunal.
The learned counsel also states that the amount awarded as compensation under all other heads is low.
4. Per contra, the submission of learned counsel for Respondent No.1 is that the Tribunal awarded excess amount as compensation.

Learned counsel states that the Tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/-
under the head love and affection and Rs.20,000/- towards miscellaneous expenses which is unjustifiable.

Learned counsel also states that the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards funeral expenses and as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC, only an amount of Rs.15,000/- is required to be awarded under the head funeral expenses.
NC: 2024:KHC:31903 5.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The judgement in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others was rendered in the year 2017.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
At para 59.8 of the said judgment the Hon'ble Apex Court observed as follows:
"59.8.
Reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs 15,000/-, Rs 40,000/- and Rs 15,000/- respectively.

The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10%
in every three years."

6. There is requirement to award a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the head loss of estate, Rs.15,000/
under the head funeral expenses and Rs.40,000/- under the head loss of consortium.
It is also clearly mentioned that the said sum has to be enhanced by 10% in every 3 years.

Therefore, as the accident occurred in the year 2020, the appellants are entitled to a sum of Rs.16,500/- per month under the head funeral expenses, Rs.16,500/- under the loss of a estate and Rs.44,000/- under the head loss of consortium.
7. Coming to the earnings of the deceased by the date of accident, admittedly no substantive proof is produced by the appellants.

However, considering the submission made by learned counsel for the appellants Sri.Girish B Baladare, this NC: 2024:KHC:31903 Court considers desirable to take the national income as Rs.14,500/- per month.
Admittedly, the deceased died at the age of 19 in the capacity of bachelor.
Thus, the multiplier to be applied is '18' and the deduction towards personal and living expenses should be 50%.

Also as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Vanajakshi vs The Manager on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45757814/
3

entities.text: Pranay Vanajakshi vs The Manager on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Sethi's Case 40% of the earnings are required to be added towards future prospects.

Thus, the loss of dependency if calculated with the above mentioned parameters, the same will be as under:
Amount Description In Rs.
 Notional Income per month 14,500-00  Annual Income (14,500X12) 1,74,000-00  Add 40% towards future 2,43,600-00  prospects (1,74,000+40%)
 Deduct 50% towards personal and living 1,21,800-00  expenses  On applying appropriate multiplier '18' 21,92,400-00 8.
As earlier discussed the appellants are also entitled to Rs.16,500 towards funeral expenses and Rs.16,500/- loss of estate.
The first appellant being mother of the deceased entitled to Rs.44,000/- towards loss of filial consortium.
This Court does not find any reasons to disturb the finding given that the appellants are entitled to Rs.3,93,500/- towards NC: 2024:KHC:31903 medical expenses.

Thus, the amount which the appellants are entitled to as compensation is as under:
 Sl. Amount  Compensation  No. in Rs.
 1 Loss of dependency 21,92,400-00  2 Funeral expenses 16,500-00  3 Loss of estate 16,500-00  4 Loss of filial consortium 44,000-00  5
Medical expenses 3,93,500-00
The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.19,75,000/-.

Thus,
the appeal is required to be allowed in part.

Therefore, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

Arakalagud, through orders in MVC No.628/2021, dated 21.03.2023 is enhanced from Rs.19,75,500/- to Rs.26,62,900/-.

(v) On such deposit, the appellants are permitted to withdraw their respective shares.
(vi) The apportionment made remains undisturbed.
